draft_key_information_units.information: Revenue increased by EUR 1.4 million (2.4%) to EUR 59.3 million in H1 2026, driven by higher charter fees from icebreaker Botnica and increased electricity sales, but operating profit fell EUR 4.7 million (25.7%) to EUR 13.6 million and profit declined EUR 4.3 million (41.7%) to EUR 6.0 million due to higher fuel/electricity costs, depreciation, lower cargo/passenger volumes, and absence of prior-year one-off gains (land sale profit and insurance indemnity). Adjusted EBITDA decreased EUR 4.0 million (13.5%) to EUR 25.8 million.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report (pages 4-5, 7-8); KPI Table (page 4); Revenue, Expenses and Profit (page 7)

draft_key_information_units.information: Operational volumes declined: cargo handling fell 5.0% to 6.5 million tonnes (mainly liquid bulk down 33.8%), passengers decreased 2.0% to 3.6 million (Tallinn-Helsinki route down 2.6%), and vessel calls dropped 4.8%. Conversely, icebreaker Botnica recorded 130 charter days (up 18.2%) with a 72% utility rate in H1 2026.

Segment revenue growth occurred in Passenger harbours (+2.9%), Ferry (+1.7%), and Other (+19.0%), while Cargo harbours fell 2.5%. Charter fee revenue rose EUR 0.9 million (18.2%) from Botnica, electricity sale revenue increased EUR 0.6 million (25.0%), and ferry services revenue grew EUR 0.3 million (1.9%). Lease income from operating leases decreased EUR 0.2 million (2.1%).

Operating expenses rose EUR 3.9 million (24.0%) in H1 2026, primarily from fuel costs up EUR 1.4 million (47.6%) due to higher prices and severe ice conditions, electricity costs up EUR 0.7 million (28.8%), and technical maintenance/repair expenses up EUR 1.2 million (80.0%). Depreciation, amortisation and impairment increased EUR 0.7 million (6.0%).

Adjusted EBITDA decreased in all segments: Cargo harbours (EUR 1.9m), Ferry (EUR 1.8m), Other (EUR 0.3m), and Passenger harbours (EUR 0.1m). The decline was driven by lower revenue, higher costs, and one-off factors (e.g., prior-year land sale gain in Cargo harbours).

Investments totalled EUR 3.5 million in H1 2026 (vs EUR 12.0 million in H1 2025), mainly for ferry engine replacement, quay upgrades at Paldiski South Harbour, and IT infrastructure. Q2 investments were EUR 2.3 million (vs EUR 8.4 million in Q2 2025).

As of 30 June 2026, total assets were EUR 615.0 million (down from EUR 622.1 million), loans and borrowings were EUR 173.4 million (stable), total liabilities were EUR 247.4 million (up from EUR 241.2 million), and equity was EUR 367.7 million (down from EUR 380.9 million). Cash and cash equivalents were EUR 27.6 million (down from EUR 32.0 million).

Significant Q2 2026 events: Tallinn City Council adopted detailed plans for Terminal A and D areas; icebreaker Botnica completed a 20-day North Sea project; a EUR 32 million unsecured loan was agreed with OP Corporate Bank; up to 485 additional Regula ferry trips were ordered for summer 2026; a EUR 19.2 million dividend was paid in Q2 2026 (85% of 2025 profit).

Market capitalisation was EUR 335.06 million at 30 June 2026 (vs EUR 340.85 million at 31 December 2025). The share price closed at EUR 1.274 on 30 June 2026 (vs EUR 1.296 at start of 2026), with 22,559 shareholders (67.0% held by the Republic of Estonia).

evaluation.selection_rationale: Units cover headline financial performance (D1), core operational volume changes and drivers (D2), segment-specific revenue dynamics (D3), major expense pressures (D4), segment profitability trends (D5), capital allocation (D6), liquidity position (D7), strategic developments and corporate actions (D8), and market valuation (D9). All are material to understanding financial performance, major period-over-period changes, and strategic developments, with explicit source support. Routine boilerplate (governance, risk lists, accounting policies) was excluded per instructions. The REFERENCE SUMMARY validated the salience of these units.
